content: Start with a cube, and [k]S,Y,1.5[/k], [k]S,Z,0.75[/k] to make a box that is 2m x 3m x 1.5m and [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] to apply the scale (Image 1).

image.caption: Image 1 - Starting with a cube, scaling it to make a box that is 2m x 3m x 1.5m and applying the scale

content: [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate the box. At this point, we need to make a decision. on the first box, select the side edges ([k]Shift-G,L[/k] will select all edges in the shape with the same length) (Image 2). Give the first box a wide bevel with six cuts, and the second box a narrow bevel with two cuts (Image 3). The first box with its wider, more rounded edges looks like its made of a formed polymer, while the second looks like welded or bent steel. For the futuristic look, we will go with the polymer style. Delete the second box and undo your changes on the first.

image.caption: Image 2 - Duplicating the box and selecting the side edges using Shift-G to select all edges of the same length
Image 3 - Giving the first box a wide bevel with six cuts for a polymer look and the second box a narrow bevel with two cuts for a welded steel look

content: Select all side edges and give it a deep bevel with one segment (Image 4). [k]Shift-G,L[/k] to select all side edges again and bevel those with six segments (Image 5). Select the bottom edge loop and bevel with six segments (Image 6).

image.caption: Image 4 - Selecting all side edges and giving it a deep bevel with one segment
Image 5 - Selecting all side edges again and beveling them with six segments
Image 6 - Selecting the bottom edge loop and beveling with six segments

content: Select the top face and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 7). In Edit Mode, [k]E,0.15[/k] to make it thicker (Image 8). In Object Mode, [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale it out, but then make minor adjustments to make the thickness even in the x- and y-axes (Image 9).

image.caption: Image 7 - Selecting the top face and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 8 - Going into Edit Mode and extruding to make it thicker
Image 9 - Going to Object Mode and scaling it out while making minor adjustments to keep the thickness even in the x- and y-axes

content: Go back to the main box, select the front face and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 10). [k]I[/k] to inset another face in the front face (Image 11). Select the outer vertices and [k]X,V[/k] to delete them and in Object Mode [k]G,X,Shift-drag[/k] to move the face out slightly in the x-axis to get rid of the z-fighting (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 10 - Going back to the main box, selecting the front face and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 11 - Insetting another face in the front face
Image 12 - Selecting the outer vertices and deleting them and then moving the face out slightly in the x-axis in Object Mode to get rid of the z-fighting

content: With the face selected, [k]E,0.1,-[/k] to extrude the face inside the box (Image 13). In Object Mode, select the box and add a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the front face as the Object (Image 14). If you hide the front face now, you will see that box now has an indentation on the front side where the front face was (Image 15). As long as we don't apply the modifier, wa can move the front face around and change the section being removed (Image 16). Get the front face object back to the center and flip any normals in that need it to fix the box (Image 17).

image.caption: Image 13 - Selecting the face and extruding it inside the box
Image 14 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the box and adding a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the front face as the Object
Image 15 - Hiding the front face to reveal the indentation on the front side of the box where the front face was
Image 16 - Moving the front face around to show how the section being removed can be changed without applying the modifier
Image 17 - Getting the front face object back to the center and flipping any normals that need it to fix the box

content: Add a Loop Cut to the front face (Image 18). Delete the left-half and add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis (Image 19). Hide the larger box (Image 20). Use the Knife Tool to cut an edge from the top corner to the bottom edge (Image 21). Bevel the edge (Image 22).

image.caption: Image 18 - Adding a Loop Cut to the front face
Image 19 - Deleting the left half and adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis
Image 20 - Hiding the larger box
Image 21 - Using the Knife Tool to cut an edge from the top corner to the bottom edge
Image 22 - Beveling the edge

content: You will need to fix the corner up top (Image 23). Extrude the vertices of the corner face in the x-, y-, and z-axes and delete the extra vertices (Image 24). Edge Slide the vertex in the corner out to close the face (Image 25). Extrude those face out in the y-axis (Image 26). Hide the front face, unhide the box and review the effect (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 23 - Fixing the corner up top
Image 24 - Extruding the vertices of the corner face in the x-, y-, and z-axes and deleting the extra vertices
Image 25 - Edge Sliding the vertex in the corner out to close the face
Image 26 - Extruding those faces out in the y-axis
Image 27 - Hiding the front face, unhiding the box and reviewing the effect

content: Hide the box again and go to work on the front face, deleting and creating faces so that in the end this is the shape we have (Image 28). Move around to the back of the front faces, set the Transform Pivot Point to Individual Origins and scale in the back faces (Image 29). Go into Vertex Select Mode and try to even out the depth on all sides (Image 30). Review the effect on the box (Image 31).

image.caption: Image 28 - Hiding the box and working on the front face, deleting and creating faces to achieve the desired shape
Image 29 - Moving to the back of the front faces, setting the Transform Pivot Point to Individual Origins and scaling in the back faces
Image 30 - Going into Vertex Select Mode and evening out the depth on all sides
Image 31 - Reviewing the effect on the box

content: We need to soften the sharp edges inside the depressions, so go around to the back, select the outer edges and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them (Image 32). Review the effect on the box again (you can really see it in Material Preview Viewport Shading) (Image 33).

image.caption: Image 32 - Going around to the back, selecting the outer edges and beveling them to soften the sharp edges inside the depressions
Image 33 - Reviewing the effect on the box in Material Preview Viewport Shading

content: Select the top face of the top and [k]Shift-D,RMB,P,S[/k] to separate it as a new object (Image 34). Go to the new top object and [k]I[/k] to inset a face (Image 35). You will have some edges that create n-gons, go to the vertices at the corners, select a group, and [k]M,A[/k] to collapse them at the center (Image 36). Repeat this all around the inset face, and merge the final corner groups to make a rectangle, and delete the outer vertices (Image 37). Move the face up slightly in the z-axis to get rid of the z-fighting (Image 38).

image.caption: Image 34 - Selecting the top face of the top and duplicating it in place and separating it as a new object
Image 35 - Going to the new top object and insetting a face
Image 36 - Going to the vertices at the corners to fix n-gons, selecting a group and collapsing them at the center
Image 37 - Repeating this all around the inset face, merging the final corner groups to make a rectangle, and deleting the outer vertices
Image 38 - Moving the face up slightly in the z-axis to get rid of the z-fighting

content: [k]E,0.1,-1[/k] to move it down into the top (Image 39). In Object Mode, select the top and add a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the top face as the Object (Image 40). Add two loop cuts to the top face to cut it into quarters, delete the opposite vertices, and add a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes (Image 41). Move the left and top edges in to create a cross shape on top (Image 42).

image.caption: Image 39 - Extruding and moving it down into the top
Image 40 - Going to Object Mode, selecting the top and adding a Boolean Modifier set to Difference with the top face as the Object
Image 41 - Adding two loop cuts to the top face to cut it into quarters, deleting the opposite vertices, and adding a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes
Image 42 - Moving the left and top edges in to create a cross shape on top

content: Fill in any missing faces (Image 43). Bevel the inner corner (Image 44). Move the middle edge inwards (Image 45). Scale in the back face and bevel the edges, like you did for the front face (Image 46).

image.caption: Image 43 - Filling in any missing faces
Image 44 - Beveling the inner corner
Image 45 - Moving the middle edge inwards
Image 46 - Scaling in the back face and beveling the edges as done for the front face

content: Duplicate and separate the side face as a new object, add a vertical Loop Cut, remove the left half, add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis, inset a small face and move it towards the top (Image 47). Delete the outside vertices, move the face out in the x-axis to fix the z-fighting, extrude inwards, and add the Boolean Modifier to the box (Image 48). Inset a small face and extrude it in (Image 49). Cut an edge on the bottom face of the extrusion and [k]S,X,0[/k] to even it out (Image 50). Extrude the bottom face up, and now you have some handles (Image 51). Feel free to bevel the inside edges if you want.

image.caption: Image 47 - Duplicating and separating the side face as a new object, adding a vertical Loop Cut, removing the left half, adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis, insetting a small face and moving it towards the top
Image 48 - Deleting the outside vertices, moving the face out in the x-axis to fix the z-fighting, extruding inwards, and adding the Boolean Modifier to the box
Image 49 - Insetting a small face and extruding it in
Image 50 - Cutting an edge on the bottom face of the extrusion and evening it out in the x-axis
Image 51 - Extruding the bottom face up to create handles

content: Add a cube to the scene and [k]S,X[/k] to scale it out in the x-axis (Image 1). Add two Loop Cuts to cut it into quarters (Image 2). Remove the left and top halves and then add a Mirror Modifier in the x-a and y-axes (Image 3). Select the right edge, extrude it out and then scale it in the y-axis (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 1 - Adding a cube to the scene and scaling it out in the x-axis
Image 2 - Adding two Loop Cuts to cut it into quarters
Image 3 - Removing the left and top halves and adding a Mirror Modifier in the x- and y-axes
Image 4 - Selecting the right edge, extruding it out and then scaling it in the y-axis

content: Extrude the edge out further and add a Loop Cut in the middle (Image 5). Grab the top edge on the end and [k]G,Z[/k] to bring it up (Image 6). Select the inner edge loop and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel it with about 4-6 segments to smooth it out (Image 7). bevel the next edge loop with 6-8 segments and make it cover a wide area (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 5 - Extruding the edge out further and adding a Loop Cut in the middle
Image 6 - Grabbing the top edge on the end and moving it up
Image 7 - Selecting the inner edge loop and beveling it with about 4-6 segments to smooth it out
Image 8 - Beveling the next edge loop with 6-8 segments to cover a wide area

content: Select the top face and [k]I,B[/k] to inset a face while keeping the borders (Image 9). [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide the bottom vertex up to make a quarter-diamond face (Image 10). Select the diamond section and [k]E[/k] to extrude it up (Image 11). Extrude up once more to create a section for the sword tip (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 9 - Selecting the top face and insetting a face while keeping the borders
Image 10 - Edge Sliding the bottom vertex up to make a quarter-diamond face
Image 11 - Selecting the diamond section and extruding it up
Image 12 - Extruding up once more to create a section for the sword tip

content: Add several Loop Cuts to the tip section (Image 13). Turn on [k]Proportional Editing > Sharp[/k] (Image 14), select the top vertices and [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale them in, making sure the Proportional Editor circle covers all vertices except the bottom (Image 15). Turn off Proportional Editing and select the top vertices and [k]M,A[/k] to merge them at center (Image 16).

image.caption: Image 13 - Adding several Loop Cuts to the tip section
Image 14 - Turning on Proportional Editing set to Sharp
Image 15 - Selecting the top vertices and scaling them in while making sure the Proportional Editor circle covers all vertices except the bottom
Image 16 - Turning off Proportional Editing, selecting the top vertices and merging them at center

content: A fuller is a rounded or beveled longitudinal groove or slot along the flat side of a blade (e.g., a sword, knife, or bayonet) that serves to both lighten and stiffen the blade, when considering its reduced weight. We will need to apply the Mirror Modifier before continuing (Image 17). We want the fuller to stop before the sword begins to curve, so add a Loop Cut to the blade somewhere below the curve (Image 18). Go down to the crossguard so you can see better, select the middle edges front and back, [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel it to a width you like and then [k]P[/k] to adjust the profile shape to curve it (Image 19). This looks good until you get to the top. Select the vertices at the top on both sides and edge slide them up (Image 20). Select the edge loop going around the blade, [k]Ctrl-B,P[/k] to bevel it and adjust the profile to curve that section (Image 21).

image.caption: Image 17 - Applying the Mirror Modifier before adding the fuller
Image 18 - Adding a Loop Cut to the blade below the curve to mark where the fuller will stop
Image 19 - Selecting the middle edges front and back, beveling to a desired width and adjusting the profile shape to curve it
Image 20 - Selecting the vertices at the top on both sides and edge sliding them up
Image 21 - Selecting the edge loop going around the blade, beveling it and adjusting the profile to curve that section

content: Select the faces underneath the crossguard and subdivide them (Image 22). Select the inner faces and [k]F[/k] to turn them into one face (Image 23). [k]Mesh > Transform > To Sphere[/k] (or [k]Shift-Alt-S[/k]) and then move your mouse to change the face at the bottom into an oval shape (Image 24). Extrude the oval face down, inset, and extrude again (Image 25).

image.caption: Image 22 - Selecting the faces underneath the crossguard and subdividing them
Image 23 - Selecting the inner faces and turning them into one face
Image 24 - Using Mesh > Transform > To Sphere and moving the mouse to change the face at the bottom into an oval shape
Image 25 - Extruding the oval face down, insetting, and extruding again

content: Add a Loop Cut to the top section and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to create some separation (Image 26). [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to create a gap (Image 27). Select the edges bevel them to make a nice rounded shape (Image 28).We want to round out the bottom face, so [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] to apply the scale and then [k]Shift-Alt-S[/k]) the bottom face into a circle shape (Image 29).

image.caption: Image 26 - Adding a Loop Cut to the top section and beveling it to create some separation
Image 27 - Extruding the faces along normals to create a gap
Image 28 - Selecting the edges and beveling them to make a nice rounded shape
Image 29 - Applying the scale and then using To Sphere to shape the bottom face into a circle

content: Add several Loop Cuts to the hilt (Image 30). Turn on [k]Proportional Editing > Smooth[/k], select the middle Loop Cut and  [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] widen the hilt (Image 31). Select the bottom face, extrude it down, select all side around the side and [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude them out along normals (Image 32). Repeat the same steps as above to add a groove in the middle and bevel the outer edges (Image 33). for the pommels, select the bottom face again, extrude it out, and then widen the bottom (Image 34).

image.caption: Image 30 - Adding several Loop Cuts to the hilt
Image 31 - Turning on Proportional Editing set to Smooth, selecting the middle Loop Cut and widening the hilt
Image 32 - Selecting the bottom face, extruding it down, selecting all sides and extruding them out along normals
Image 33 - Repeating the same steps to add a groove in the middle and bevel the outer edges
Image 34 - Selecting the bottom face again, extruding it out and widening the bottom for the pommel

content: Select the bottom face of the pommel and inset it (Image 35). Select all edges around that inner face (Image 36). [k]RMB,S[/k] to subdivide them (Image 37).

image.caption: Image 35 - Selecting the bottom face of the pommel and insetting it
Image 36 - Selecting all edges around that inner face
Image 37 - Subdividing those edges

content: Turn on [k]Proportional Editing > Sphere[/k], select the inner face and [k]G,Z[/k] to bring it down in a rounded shape (Image 38). Round out the top of the pommel by adding a Loop Cut (image 39). Scale it in (Image 40). And Bevel it (image 41).

image.caption: Image 38 - Turning on Proportional Editing set to Sphere, selecting the inner face and bringing it down in a rounded shape
Image 39 - Rounding out the top of the pommel by adding a Loop Cut
Image 40 - Scaling it in
Image 41 - Beveling it

content: Select all edges you want to use for the wrapped handle and bevel them (Image 42). Select the top edge loops of all the bevels and [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to bring them out (Image 43). [k]G,Z[/k] the edges down so they overlap the ones underneath (Image 44). Shift-Select the inner edge loops under the folds (Image 45). [k]Ctrl-Alt-Shift-S[/k] to use the [k]Shear Tool[/k] and [k]Y[/k] to limit it to the y-axis (Image 46).

image.caption: Image 42 - Selecting all edges to use for the wrapped handle and beveling them
Image 43 - Selecting the top edge loops of all the bevels and bringing them out
Image 44 - Moving the edges down so they overlap the ones underneath
Image 45 - Shift-selecting the inner edge loops under the folds
Image 46 - Using the Shear Tool and limiting it to the y-axis

content: Start with a Cylinder, however many vertices you like, and [k]S,Shift-Z[/k] to scale it in the x- and y-axes (Image 1). We want to make the pommel and crossguard so [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add three Loop Cuts (Image 2). Select the face loops by the cuts and [k]Alt-E,F[/k] to extrude them out evenly (Image 3).

Add a cube, scale it down, and move it into position at the top of the shaft (Image 4). Select the two outside edges of the cube (Image 5). [k]RMB,S[/k] to subdivide it with three cuts (Image 6). Select the edge second from the top and [k]G,G[/k] to slide it up (Image 7). Select the top edge and slide it back (Image 8). We want to move the bottom face back as well, but keep it lined up with the top, so select the bottom face and [k]G[/k] to move it, [k]B[/k] to activate Snap Base and choose the top edge (Image 9). This will restrict movement so that you can align with the top. Select the two edges on the outside of the bottom face and [k]RMB,S[/k] to subdivide it (Image 10). Slide the bottom edge in to make a sort of butterfly shape (Image 11).

[k]Tab[/k] into Object Mode and [k]Ctrl-A,S[/k] to apply the scale, if you don't the bevel won't apply evenly (Image 12). Select the outside edges (Image 13). [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them, but not all the way since this is an energy weapon, not a weapon designed to penetrate armour (Image 14). Change the Transform Pivot Point to 3D Cursor (Image 15), and [k]Alt-D,R,90[/k] to create four linked duplicates rotated around the haft (Image 16). Make any adjustments to the flange's geometry in Edit Mode, and it will be applied to all (Image 17).

Add a new Cylinder, and scale it down so it covers the top part of the haft, give it a rotation and apply ([k]Ctrl-A,R[/k] (Image 18). Add a Cube to the scene, scale and mirror so it covers part of the new cylinder evenly on two sides (Image 19). Go into Local View with the cube ([k]/[/k]) and update the shape using [k]G[/k], [k]Ctrl-B[/k] (Image 20). Add a Boolean Modifier to the cylinder with the cube as the target object (Image 21). Apply the modifier to the cube and move one side down to create some difference (Image 22).

Change the Transform Pivot Point back to the 3D Cursor, select a flange and [k]Alt-D,R,45[/k] (Image 23). Add three more (Image 24). The flanges are running over each other, so select one, and in Edit Mode scale in the thickness (Image 25). Select the four corner flanges, set the Transform Pivot Point to Individual Origins and scale them in Edit Mode to make them smaller (Image 26).
Add a Cube to the side with the longer covering and scale it down (Image 27). Apply the scale and bevel the bottom edge (Image 28). Bevel the edges on the sides (Image 29).

Add a new Cube and scale it down so it is a thin cube embedded in the power unit (Image 30). Go into Local View and [k]B,C[/k] to bevel the bottom edges and clamp it, creating a rounded end (Image 31). Exit Local View and add an Array Modifier in the z-axis (Image 32). [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate the power unit, and leave it in place (Image 33). Add a Boolean Modifier to the power unit with the rounded-end wedges as the target; hide the rounded-end wedges (Image 34). Select the duplicate power unit and scale it down (Image 35). We want a separator for our vents, so go back to the wedge mesh, and add a Loop Cut down the middle (Image 36). Bevel the edge loop until you reach the desired thickness, delete the faces and fill in the gaps (Image 37). Hide the wedges again (Image 38). Select the inner mesh, cutting round wedges, and parent the outer power unit to them, so that if you move the power unit, the other pieces come with it (Image 39).

Add several Loop Cuts to the grip (Image 40). Select all faces in the grip, and [k]I,I[/k] to inset faces individually (Image 41). Inset the faces again, but this time use [k]Ctrl[/k] to affect the depth (Image 42).

Select a face along the bottom of the grip and [k]Shift-S,T[/k] to position the 3D Cursor (Image 43). Add an Ico Sphere to the scene and scale it down (Image 44). [k]Shift-S,W[/k] to move the 3D Cursor back to the World Origin, set the Transform Pivot Point to 3D Cursor, and [k]Alt-D,R,90[/k] to make four studs around the bottom (Image 45). Repeat these steps at the top of the grip (Image 46). Add two more studs up by the power unit (Image 47).
